title: Peatlands and the Paradox of Slow Decay
body:
Peatlands occupy barely three percent of the global land surface, yet the carbon locked in their saturated soils exceeds the amount held in every forest on the planet combined. This disproportion arises not from exceptional productivity but from exceptionally slow decay. In most terrestrial ecosystems, the organic matter that plants deposit each year is almost entirely consumed by microbes within a decade. In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually. Most northern peat began forming as the last ice sheets withdrew, and the deposits have been thickening, almost imperceptibly, ever since.

The mechanism behind this arrested breakdown is chemical as much as physical. Because water fills the pore spaces that would otherwise hold air, oxygen diffuses through peat far more slowly than through dry soil, and the aerobic bacteria responsible for rapid decay are confined to a thin surface layer. Sphagnum mosses, the dominant peat-forming plants of northern bogs, compound this constraint: they actively acidify their surroundings and release phenolic compounds that inhibit the enzymes microbes secrete in order to dismantle complex organic molecules. Ecologists call this self-reinforcing arrangement the enzymic latch, a metaphor that captures how a modest chemical brake can hold an entire carbon reservoir in place.

The latch, however, is easily released. When peatlands are drained for pasture, forestry, or fuel extraction, the water table falls, oxygen penetrates layers that have been sealed for millennia, and microbial respiration resumes at rates the system has not experienced since the deposits first formed. The surface subsides, sometimes by several centimeters a year, and carbon that accumulated over ten thousand years can be returned to the atmosphere within a single human lifetime. Drained peat also becomes combustible. The smoldering fires that periodically blanket parts of Southeast Asia in haze burn downward through dried deposits rather than across the canopy, which is precisely why conventional firefighting has so little effect on them.

Restoration therefore concentrates on hydrology rather than on planting. Blocking drainage ditches allows the water table to recover, and Sphagnum, once reestablished, gradually restores the chemical conditions that suppress decay. The remedy is not without ambiguity: rewetted peat emits methane, a gas whose warming effect over two decades far surpasses that of carbon dioxide, and some restored sites consequently aggravate warming before they alleviate it. Most researchers nevertheless regard the trade-off as favorable, because methane persists in the atmosphere for roughly a decade whereas the carbon dioxide released by continued oxidation would linger for centuries. Restoration is correspondingly slow, since a bog that required eight thousand years to build cannot be reconstituted within a decade. The arithmetic of peatland management thus depends less on annual accounting than on the horizon over which the accounting is done.

questions.question: According to paragraph 2, why does oxygen move through peat much more slowly than through dry soil?

choices.A: Sphagnum mosses consume the available oxygen as they grow.
choices.B: Water occupies the pore spaces that would otherwise contain air.
choices.C: The acidity of the peat chemically binds oxygen to organic molecules.
choices.D: A thin surface layer of bacteria blocks oxygen from descending.

questions.explanation: 第2段落に "Because water fills the pore spaces that would otherwise hold air, oxygen diffuses through peat far more slowly than through dry soil" とあり、原因は水が空気の入る隙間を満たしていることだと明示されている。Aは本文に記述がない。Cは酸性化について述べているが、酸性化の効果は酵素の阻害であって酸素の結合ではない。Dは因果が逆で、好気性細菌が表層に限られるのは酸素不足の結果である。

questions.question: The word "arrested" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: "arrested breakdown" は第1段落の "decomposition stalls" を言い換えた表現であり、分解が止まっている状態を指す。したがって halted が最も近い。B の detected（発見する）と D の measured（測定する）は arrest の法的・計測的な連想からの誤答で、文脈上の「止まる」という意味を持たない。C の accelerated は意味が正反対である。

questions.question: The word "they" in paragraph 2 ("they actively acidify their surroundings") refers to
questions.explanation: コロンの前にある主節の主語は "Sphagnum mosses" で、"the dominant peat-forming plants of northern bogs" はその同格説明である。コロン以降の節はその苔がどのように制約を強めるかを具体化している。B の好気性細菌は前の文の主語だが、酸性化を行う主体としては述べられていない。C の northern bogs は所属を示す修飾句の一部にすぎない。D の phenolic compounds は they が放出する対象であり、they 自身ではない。

questions.question: What can be inferred from paragraph 3 about the rate at which peat stores and loses carbon?

choices.A: Carbon is lost from drained peat at roughly the same rate at which it originally accumulated.
choices.B: Peat that has been drained will eventually stop losing carbon once its surface stops subsiding.
choices.C: Loss of carbon after drainage proceeds far faster than the accumulation that preceded it.
choices.D: Peatlands release most of their carbon through fire rather than through microbial respiration.

questions.explanation: 第3段落に "carbon that accumulated over ten thousand years can be returned to the atmosphere within a single human lifetime" とあり、一万年かけて蓄積した炭素が人間の一生のうちに放出されうる、つまり放出は蓄積より桁違いに速いと推論できる。A は本文の対比を無視している。B は表面沈下が止まれば炭素損失も止まるという因果を本文は述べていない。D は火災と微生物呼吸のどちらが主要かを本文は比較していない。

questions.question: Why does the author mention the smoldering fires that blanket parts of Southeast Asia in haze?

choices.A: To argue that fire suppression should be the main priority of peatland policy
choices.B: To identify the original cause of drainage in tropical peatlands
choices.C: To contrast tropical peatlands with the northern bogs described earlier
choices.D: To illustrate an additional consequence of drainage that ordinary firefighting cannot address

questions.explanation: この文は "Drained peat also becomes combustible." に続いて置かれており、also が示す通り排水がもたらす追加の帰結を具体化している。さらに "burn downward through dried deposits rather than across the canopy, which is precisely why conventional firefighting has so little effect on them" と、通常の消火が効かない理由まで説明している。A は政策の優先順位を本文は主張していない。B は火災は排水の結果であって原因ではないため因果が逆。C は南北の泥炭地の比較が本段落の論点ではない。

peatlands.etymology: peat（泥炭）+ land（土地）+ -s（複数）。peat は中世ラテン語 peta「泥炭の一片」に遡る。
peatlands.definition: 泥炭が厚く堆積した湿地。
peatlands.usage_in_passage: 冒頭 "Peatlands occupy barely three percent of the global land surface" で本文全体の主題を提示し、面積の小ささと貯蔵炭素量の大きさという逆説を立ち上げる。
peatlands.context_sentence: Peatlands occupy barely three percent of the global land surface, yet the carbon locked in their saturated soils exceeds the amount held in every forest on the planet combined.

occupy.etymology: ラテン語 occupare = ob-（〜に向かって）+ capere（つかむ）。「先に取る」から「場所を占める」へ。
occupy.usage_in_passage: "Peatlands occupy barely three percent" と面積比を提示し、直後の yet による逆接を準備する。
occupy.context_sentence: Peatlands occupy barely three percent of the global land surface, yet the carbon locked in their saturated soils exceeds the amount held in every forest on the planet combined.

barely.etymology: 古英語 bær（むき出しの）+ -ly（副詞化）。「裸同然に」から「かろうじて」へ。
barely.definition: ほんのわずかしか〜ない。
barely.usage_in_passage: "barely three percent" と数値を最小方向に強調し、次に来る「全森林を超える炭素量」との落差を大きくする。
barely.context_sentence: Peatlands occupy barely three percent of the global land surface, yet the carbon locked in their saturated soils exceeds the amount held in every forest on the planet combined.

carbon.etymology: ラテン語 carbo「炭・燃えさし」+ -on（元素名の接尾辞）。
carbon.definition: 炭素。有機物と二酸化炭素の主要構成元素。
carbon.usage_in_passage: "the carbon locked in their saturated soils" が本文の中心概念で、蓄積（第1・2段落）と放出（第3段落）という論の軸をなす。
carbon.context_sentence: Peatlands occupy barely three percent of the global land surface, yet the carbon locked in their saturated soils exceeds the amount held in every forest on the planet combined.

locked.definition: 閉じ込められて動かせない状態にされた。
locked.usage_in_passage: "the carbon locked in their saturated soils" は炭素が循環から外れて固定されていることを錠前の比喩で表し、第2段落の enzymic latch、第3段落の "easily released" と一連の比喩を作る。
locked.context_sentence: Peatlands occupy barely three percent of the global land surface, yet the carbon locked in their saturated soils exceeds the amount held in every forest on the planet combined.

saturated.etymology: ラテン語 satur「満ちた」+ -ate（動詞化）+ -ed。
saturated.definition: 水を含みきって飽和した。
saturated.usage_in_passage: "saturated soils" が分解を止める物理条件を最初に示し、第2段落の pore spaces の説明の伏線となる。
saturated.context_sentence: Peatlands occupy barely three percent of the global land surface, yet the carbon locked in their saturated soils exceeds the amount held in every forest on the planet combined.

soils.etymology: 古フランス語 soil < ラテン語 solum「地面」+ -s。
soils.usage_in_passage: "saturated soils" として炭素の貯蔵場所を指し、後出の "dry soil" と対比される。
soils.context_sentence: Peatlands occupy barely three percent of the global land surface, yet the carbon locked in their saturated soils exceeds the amount held in every forest on the planet combined.

exceeds.etymology: ラテン語 ex-（外へ）+ cedere（行く）→「越え出る」+ -s。
exceeds.usage_in_passage: "exceeds the amount held in every forest on the planet combined" が第1文の逆接の核であり、面積比と貯蔵量の不均衡を成立させる。
exceeds.context_sentence: Peatlands occupy barely three percent of the global land surface, yet the carbon locked in their saturated soils exceeds the amount held in every forest on the planet combined.

disproportion.etymology: dis-（否定）+ pro-（前に）+ ラテン語 portio「割合」。
disproportion.definition: 釣り合いの取れていない状態。
disproportion.usage_in_passage: "This disproportion arises not from..." と直前の対比全体を一語で受け直し、現象の提示から原因の説明へ論を橋渡しする指示的抽象名詞。
disproportion.context_sentence: This disproportion arises not from exceptional productivity but from exceptionally slow decay.

arises.etymology: 古英語 ā-（強意の接頭辞）+ risan（立ち上がる）+ -s。
arises.usage_in_passage: "arises not from X but from Y" の構文で誤った原因を先に排除し、正しい原因を際立たせる。
arises.context_sentence: This disproportion arises not from exceptional productivity but from exceptionally slow decay.

exceptional.etymology: ラテン語 ex-（外へ）+ capere（取る）→ except「除外する」+ -ion + -al。
exceptional.usage_in_passage: "not from exceptional productivity" と否定される側に置かれ、読者が抱きがちな「生産量が多いから炭素が多い」という推測を封じる。
exceptional.context_sentence: This disproportion arises not from exceptional productivity but from exceptionally slow decay.

productivity.etymology: ラテン語 pro-（前へ）+ ducere（導く）→ produce + -ivity（性質を表す）。
productivity.definition: 生産力。生態学では単位時間あたりの有機物生産量。
productivity.usage_in_passage: 泥炭地の炭素量の原因ではないものとして否定され、代わりに decay の遅さが原因として提示される。
productivity.context_sentence: This disproportion arises not from exceptional productivity but from exceptionally slow decay.

exceptionally.usage_in_passage: "exceptionally slow decay" と肯定される側の原因を強め、直前の exceptional productivity と語形をそろえることで否定と肯定の対比を音の上でも際立たせる。
exceptionally.context_sentence: This disproportion arises not from exceptional productivity but from exceptionally slow decay.

decay.etymology: ラテン語 de-（下へ）+ cadere（落ちる）。「落ちぶれる」から「腐敗する」へ。
decay.definition: 有機物が微生物によって分解されること。
decay.usage_in_passage: "exceptionally slow decay" が本文の主因であり、第2段落の enzymic latch はこの遅さの説明として導入される。
decay.context_sentence: This disproportion arises not from exceptional productivity but from exceptionally slow decay.

terrestrial.usage_in_passage: "In most terrestrial ecosystems" と一般則の適用範囲を示し、次文の泥炭地という例外を際立たせる。
terrestrial.context_sentence: In most terrestrial ecosystems, the organic matter that plants deposit each year is almost entirely consumed by microbes within a decade.

ecosystems.etymology: ギリシャ語 oikos「家」→ eco- + system「組み合わさったもの」+ -s。
ecosystems.definition: 生態系。生物とその環境からなる機能単位。
ecosystems.usage_in_passage: 泥炭地を他の生態系と比較する枠組みを与え、比較のうえで例外性を示す論の型を作る。
ecosystems.context_sentence: In most terrestrial ecosystems, the organic matter that plants deposit each year is almost entirely consumed by microbes within a decade.

organic.etymology: ギリシャ語 organon「道具・器官」+ -ic。
organic.definition: 生物に由来する、炭素化合物からなる。
organic.usage_in_passage: "the organic matter that plants deposit each year" で分解の対象物を特定し、炭素の出入りを追う準備をする。
organic.context_sentence: In most terrestrial ecosystems, the organic matter that plants deposit each year is almost entirely consumed by microbes within a decade.

deposit.etymology: ラテン語 de-（下に）+ ponere「置く」。
deposit.usage_in_passage: "the organic matter that plants deposit each year" と動詞で供給側を示し、第1段落末と第3段落の名詞 deposits（堆積層）と対をなす。
deposit.context_sentence: In most terrestrial ecosystems, the organic matter that plants deposit each year is almost entirely consumed by microbes within a decade.

entirely.etymology: ラテン語 integer「手つかずの」→ 古フランス語 entier + -ly。
entirely.usage_in_passage: "almost entirely consumed by microbes within a decade" と通常の生態系での分解の徹底ぶりを強調し、泥炭地の stalls との落差を作る。
entirely.context_sentence: In most terrestrial ecosystems, the organic matter that plants deposit each year is almost entirely consumed by microbes within a decade.

consumed.etymology: ラテン語 con-（すっかり）+ sumere「取る」+ -ed。
consumed.definition: 食い尽くされる、消費される。
consumed.usage_in_passage: 微生物が有機物を残さず処理することを示し、直後の "decomposition stalls" と正面から対照される。
consumed.context_sentence: In most terrestrial ecosystems, the organic matter that plants deposit each year is almost entirely consumed by microbes within a decade.

microbes.etymology: ギリシャ語 mikros「小さい」+ bios「生命」+ -s。
microbes.usage_in_passage: 分解の主体として導入され、第2段落で "the enzymes microbes secrete" として再登場し、抑制の対象になる。
microbes.context_sentence: In most terrestrial ecosystems, the organic matter that plants deposit each year is almost entirely consumed by microbes within a decade.

decade.usage_in_passage: "within a decade" が通常の分解の時間尺度を与え、第3段落の "ten thousand years" や最終段落のメタンの寿命と比較される基準になる。
decade.context_sentence: In most terrestrial ecosystems, the organic matter that plants deposit each year is almost entirely consumed by microbes within a decade.

waterlogged.etymology: water + log（水を吸って丸太のように動かなくなる船の状態）+ -ed。
waterlogged.definition: 水浸しで排水されていない。
waterlogged.usage_in_passage: "In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast" と例外が成立する条件を明示し、以降の説明の前提を固定する。
waterlogged.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

peatland.usage_in_passage: 複数形 peatlands が一般論を指すのに対し、ここでは単数形で典型例を取り出し、個々の場所で何が起きるかを描写する。
peatland.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

contrast.etymology: ラテン語 contra-（対して）+ stare「立つ」。
contrast.usage_in_passage: "by contrast" は一般則から例外への転換を読者に予告する談話標識で、第1段落の論理構造を可視化している。
contrast.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

decomposition.etymology: de-（分離）+ com-（共に）+ ponere「置く」→ compose の逆 + -ition。
decomposition.definition: 分解。有機物が無機物に戻る過程。
decomposition.usage_in_passage: "decomposition stalls" が本文の中心現象を名詞で提示し、第2段落で "arrested breakdown" と言い換えられる。
decomposition.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

stalls.etymology: 古英語 steall「立ち位置」→「立ち止まる」+ -s。
stalls.definition: 途中で止まる、進まなくなる。
stalls.usage_in_passage: "decomposition stalls" は第2段落冒頭の "arrested breakdown" と言い換え関係にあり、語彙問題 arrested の解答根拠になる。
stalls.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

successive.etymology: ラテン語 sub-（下に）+ cedere「行く」→ succeed + -ive。
successive.usage_in_passage: "successive generations of vegetation accumulate" と時間の積み重ねを示し、archive という比喩に厚みを与える。
successive.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

vegetation.etymology: ラテン語 vegetare「活気づける」+ -ation。
vegetation.definition: 植生。ある地域の植物の総体。
vegetation.usage_in_passage: 堆積する材料の実体を指し、直後の "a dark, fibrous archive" が何でできているかを読者に理解させる。
vegetation.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

accumulate.etymology: ラテン語 ad-（〜へ）+ cumulus「積み重ね」+ -ate。
accumulate.usage_in_passage: 蓄積側の中心動詞で、第3段落の過去形 accumulated と対応し、蓄積と損失の速度差という設問4の論点を作る。
accumulate.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

fibrous.usage_in_passage: "a dark, fibrous archive" と泥炭の見た目を描写しつつ、植物組織が分解されずに残っていることを含意する。
fibrous.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

deepen.etymology: deep + -en（形容詞を動詞化する接尾辞）。
deepen.usage_in_passage: "may deepen by less than a millimeter annually" と蓄積速度を数値化し、第3段落の沈下速度と桁で比較できるようにする。
deepen.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

millimeter.etymology: ラテン語 mille「千」+ ギリシャ語 metron「尺度」。1メートルの千分の一。
millimeter.usage_in_passage: 年間の堆積量を示す単位で、第3段落の "several centimeters a year" という沈下速度と対比され、蓄積の遅さを際立たせる。
millimeter.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

annually.usage_in_passage: 堆積を年率で示し、最終段落の "annual accounting" という時間尺度の議論に接続する。
annually.context_sentence: In a waterlogged peatland, by contrast, decomposition stalls, and successive generations of vegetation accumulate as a dark, fibrous archive that may deepen by less than a millimeter annually.

peat.etymology: 中世ラテン語 peta「泥炭の一片」。
peat.definition: 泥炭。分解しきらない植物遺体が堆積したもの。
peat.usage_in_passage: "Most northern peat began forming" と不可算名詞で素材そのものを指し、場所を指す peatland と使い分けられている。
peat.context_sentence: Most northern peat began forming as the last ice sheets withdrew, and the deposits have been thickening, almost imperceptibly, ever since.

withdrew.etymology: with-（後方へ）+ draw「引く」の過去形。
withdrew.usage_in_passage: "as the last ice sheets withdrew" と泥炭形成の開始時点を最終氷期の終わりに位置づけ、蓄積が地質学的な時間尺度をもつことを示す。
withdrew.context_sentence: Most northern peat began forming as the last ice sheets withdrew, and the deposits have been thickening, almost imperceptibly, ever since.

deposits.usage_in_passage: "the deposits have been thickening" と動詞から名詞へ転じ、第3段落では "sealed for millennia" される対象として再登場する。
deposits.context_sentence: Most northern peat began forming as the last ice sheets withdrew, and the deposits have been thickening, almost imperceptibly, ever since.

thickening.definition: 厚みを増していくこと。
thickening.usage_in_passage: 現在完了進行形の中で用いられ、氷期の終わりから現在まで途切れず続く緩慢な蓄積を表す。
thickening.context_sentence: Most northern peat began forming as the last ice sheets withdrew, and the deposits have been thickening, almost imperceptibly, ever since.

imperceptibly.etymology: im-（否定）+ per-（通して）+ capere「取る」→ perceive + -ible + -ly。
imperceptibly.definition: 知覚できないほどわずかに。
imperceptibly.usage_in_passage: "almost imperceptibly" と millimeter の数値を感覚のことばで言い換え、蓄積の遅さを二重に印象づける。
imperceptibly.context_sentence: Most northern peat began forming as the last ice sheets withdrew, and the deposits have been thickening, almost imperceptibly, ever since.

mechanism.definition: 現象を成り立たせている仕組み。
mechanism.usage_in_passage: "The mechanism behind this arrested breakdown" が第2段落の主題文で、現象の記述から原因の説明へ論を切り替える。
mechanism.context_sentence: The mechanism behind this arrested breakdown is chemical as much as physical.

arrested.etymology: ラテン語 ad-（〜に）+ restare「とどまる」→ 古フランス語 arester + -ed。
arrested.definition: 途中で停止させられた。
arrested.usage_in_passage: "this arrested breakdown" は第1段落の "decomposition stalls" を受け直した言い換えであり、語彙問題の対象語となっている。
arrested.context_sentence: The mechanism behind this arrested breakdown is chemical as much as physical.

breakdown.usage_in_passage: decomposition の平易な言い換えとして使われ、同じ概念を別の語で受けることで学術文特有の語彙変換を読者に要求する。
breakdown.context_sentence: The mechanism behind this arrested breakdown is chemical as much as physical.

pore.usage_in_passage: "the pore spaces that would otherwise hold air" が酸素不足の物理的原因を特定しており、設問1の直接の根拠になる。
pore.context_sentence: Because water fills the pore spaces that would otherwise hold air, oxygen diffuses through peat far more slowly than through dry soil, and the aerobic bacteria responsible for rapid decay are confined to a thin surface layer.

oxygen.etymology: ギリシャ語 oxys「酸っぱい」+ -gen「生む」。酸の素と誤解された命名。
